title: Atlas · Mon Nov 23 · 6:45am
big_picture: Futures are sharply higher: Nasdaq-100 up about 3.6%, S&P 500 up about 2.8%, Dow up about 2% in the 5:19am ET update ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/23/futures-rally-after-wall-streets-nightmare-week-.html)). Friday's close is the base: S&P 500 6,910, down 8.6% on the week, VIX 35.9. Two things are being named. First, President Trump posted on Truth Social that he hopes Nvidia's board rehires Jensen Huang, and Nvidia is up about 7-9% pre-market; but Nvidia's chair said the board "unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate" him, and a prediction market puts a return at 16% ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/nvidia-stock-jumps-as-dc-makes-stunning-u-turn-on-jensen-huang-113419437.html), [Tokenist](https://tokenist.com/nvidia-stock-trump-huang-return-bessent/)). That is a political headline, not a change in Nvidia's business. Second, a calmer backdrop: the 2-year Treasury yield fell to about 4.61% and Asian authorities (South Korea, China) propped up their markets ([Saxo](https://www.home.saxo/en-sg/content/articles/macro/asia-market-quick-take--23-november-2026-23112026), [Reuters via Investing.com](https://za.investing.com/news/economy-news/us-futures-rally-as-ai-rout-pauses-asian-authorities-prop-up-stocks-4591490)). Gold is up about 2.5% to near $3,620 after a one-year low on Friday, Brent is down about 4% to roughly $88-91 on supply-surplus worries, and bitcoin sits near $61,500 ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/us-futures-bounce-while-asia-234419517.html), [JournalArta](https://journalarta.com/en/2026/11/23/stock-market-today-dow-sp-500-futures-surge-after-tech-rout-as-oil-slides/)). The Fed still looks set to hike on Dec 9 (above 90% odds) ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/23/futures-rally-after-wall-streets-nightmare-week-.html)). Prices below are Friday's close (my price files), pre-market moves are from EODHD quotes at about 6:55am Pacific and will have moved.

- MU / MU.TO: MU.TO closed 25.97 CAD, -13.8% Friday. That answers my "stale price" question: the file had lagged by one day. Micron's next report is Dec 17 (per Yahoo Finance, not in my files). Pre-market MU is +4.8%.
Taylor, nothing here needs a decision before the open; the one to watch is MU.

Bottom watch (you asked for signs the sell-off is lifting): Met: extreme fear (Fear & Greed 10 on Friday), VIX above 35, heavy selling by trend-followers, and this morning the 2-year yield is falling. Missing: no reversal day yet (Friday closed near its low), AAII is not extreme (bears 42.2%, bulls 33.3%, survey closed before Friday's close), and credit is not in panic but is widening: one source has the ICE BofA high-yield spread at 3.52% from 3.20% a week earlier, Saxo cites 367 basis points, the highest since early 2025. I'd call it "relief bounce possible, bottom not confirmed". Sources: [Saxo](https://www.home.saxo/content/articles/macro/market-quick-take---sentiment-bounces-after-friday-mayhem---23-november-2026-23112026), [Cycledesk](https://cycledesk.substack.com/p/have-we-seen-the-bottom-and-what), [Kalkine](https://kalkine.ca/news/economic-news/is-the-high-yield-credit-spread-widening-currently-at-343-after-a-20-basis-point-rise). notes: Morning, Taylor. After the worst week in about 18 months, this is a bounce morning, and I would treat it as a bounce until something else proves it. Your Micron is the name to watch at the open.
Pre-market movers (EODHD, vs Friday's close):

- NVDA 136.27 (+7.9%), MU 624.63 (+4.8%), TSM 337.50 (+5.6%), CRWV 42.00 (+5.9%), SMH 422.50 (+5.3%), QQQ +3.2%, SPY +2.4%. MU is still under the $650 line (Nov 5 low) that was the kill line in the old AI-build-out view.

- CrowdStrike agreed to buy Zscaler for $43.9B in stock ($260.41 a share, a 34% premium to Friday). Zscaler is up about 16% pre-market and CrowdStrike down about 8% ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/23/futures-rally-after-wall-streets-nightmare-week-.html), [MLQ](https://mlq.ai/news/nasdaq-futures-rise-3-and-nvidia-gains-9-premarket-as-zscaler-jumps-20-on-crowdstrikes-offer/)). That is a business event: the buyer is paying up and its own holders take the dilution.

- Memory names are up on Citi saying AI-spending fears are overdone ([Invezz](https://invezz.com/ie/news/2026/11/23/micron-sandisk-climb-in-premarket-as-citi-strikes-optimistic-tone-on-memory-stocks/)). An analyst note and a rebound are not a turn; MarketBeat itself calls it a relief bounce.

What to watch at the 7:30am open: whether the pre-market gains hold or fade in the first 30 minutes (wait 15-30 minutes before reading anything into it), whether MU can get above $650 on real volume ([TradingKey](https://www.tradingkey.com/analysis/stocks/us-stocks/262317982-stock-microm-mu-price-650-ai-vix-tradingkey)), and whether the VIX closes lower than Friday's 35.9.
What I dug into:

- CoreWeave and Nvidia (t20261114-L3, t20261115-L1; still open): CoreWeave's Q3 10-Q debt note shows about $46.9B of debt at Sep 30, 2026, and one third-party reading of its maturity table has about $2.4B due in the rest of 2026 and $11.0B in 2027 (not checked by me against the filing). The 10-Q calls it a take-or-pay business (98% of Q3 revenue per one source) and says top-two customers were 54% (secondary source). Nvidia's share of CoreWeave's revenue is still not found. Sources: [CoreWeave 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001769628/000176962826000465/crwv-20260930.htm), [CCIR Research](https://ccir.io/research/coreweave-debt-by-entity-q3-2026), [Converge Digest](https://convergedigest.com/coreweave-q3-2026-earnings-financing-nvidia-backlog/). I read search summaries; the filing page itself did not open here.

- Commerce chip rule and MU/TSM (t20261116-4, t20261117-1; still open): nothing new today beyond what I had: the rule needs licences for Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil, Micron had about $14.6B of China-linked revenue last fiscal year by customer headquarters, and the share that the rule actually touches is still not found ([24/7 Wall St](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/11/16/micron-has-14-6-billion-in-china-linked-revenue-are-these-new-u-s-chip-export-rules-a-threat/)).
- What a real bottom looks like (t20261121-L1; still open): see Bottom watch above.
EODHD was used for pre-market quotes only.

Trend board changes: AI build-out stays closed (kill hit Friday); evidence added: pre-market rebound with MU 624.63 still under 650. Cyber bounce stays "watching": CrowdStrike buying Zscaler for $43.9B in stock is a fact that supports the idea that big security vendors are consolidating, but one deal is not a trend and CRWD is down about 8% on it. Rate-hike pressure stays "watching": hike odds still above 90%, but the 2-year yield fell this morning, which is the first softening I have seen.
